html:
An East Germanic people related to the Goths, who lived in and around the Carpathian basin from the 3rd to the 6th century. The map shows them in 400, placed north of the Carpathians in what is now western Ukraine.

Under the Huns they were among Attila's most trusted subjects. After Attila's death their king Ardaric led the subject peoples in revolt and beat the Huns at the Battle of Nedao in 454, ending Hun power in Europe. The Gepids then held the eastern Carpathian basin, in what is now eastern Hungary, Romania and Serbia, and in the 6th century took the old Roman city of Sirmium.

They fought the Lombards to their west for decades, with Byzantium switching support between the two. In 567 the Lombards and the Avars crushed them, and the Lombard king Alboin is said to have made a drinking cup from the Gepid king's skull. The Gepids then faded away under Avar rule. Their language and their Arian Christianity were shared with the Goths.
